objective: Report orders that have waited too long to ship. `OrderBook` (in `stockroom/orders.py`) gets `awaiting(as_of: date, days: int) -> list[Order]`, the overdue orders. Only orders with status `open` or `paid` can be overdue (shipped and cancelled orders never are), and an order placed after `as_of` is never overdue. An order is overdue when it was placed more than `days` days before `as_of`, counted in whole days with `dates.days_between(placed, as_of)`: an order placed exactly `days` days before `as_of` is not overdue yet, and one placed `days + 1` days before is. So with `days` 0 every open or paid order placed before `as_of` is overdue, but not one placed on `as_of`. A negative `days` raises `ValueError` (also for an empty book). The result is oldest placement date first; orders placed on the same day come in plain string order of `order_id` (Python `str` comparison, so `V-10` comes before `V-9`). The CLI gets `python -m stockroom overdue --orders FILE --as-of YYYY-MM-DD [--days N]` with `--days` defaulting to 7. It prints one line per overdue order in that order, `ID CUSTOMER: placed YYYY-MM-DD, AGE old, AMOUNT`, where AGE is `textutil.plural(n, "day")` for the whole days from placement to `as_of` and AMOUNT is the order's subtotal (`pricing.order_subtotal`) formatted by `money.format_money` with the configured `currency_symbol`; then a last line `COUNT, TOTAL in total`, where COUNT is `textutil.plural(count, "overdue order")` and TOTAL is the formatted sum of the listed subtotals (`0 overdue orders, $0.00 in total` when there are none). A negative `--days` is a data error with the message `--days must not be negative`, and an `--as-of` that is not a date gives the `not a date: ...` message of `dates.parse_date`; data errors exit with code 1, print nothing on stdout and print `stockroom: error: MESSAGE` on stderr. The other commands are unchanged.
acceptance: `awaiting` treats an order as overdue only when `days_between(placed, as_of)` is greater than `days` (exactly `days` days is not overdue, `days + 1` is; with 0 an order placed on `as_of` is not overdue), and raises `ValueError` for a negative `days`, also on an empty book
Over many seeded random books, `awaiting` returns exactly the open or paid orders older than `days` days, oldest first and ties by `order_id` in plain string order
Shipped and cancelled orders and orders placed after `as_of` are never overdue, and an empty book gives `[]`
Orders placed on the same day are listed in plain string order of `order_id` (`V-10` before `V-9`), after older orders

`overdue` prints `ID CUSTOMER: placed DATE, AGE old, AMOUNT` per overdue order and `COUNT, TOTAL in total`, with `plural` for AGE and COUNT, `--days` defaulting to 7 and amounts in the configured currency symbol
`overdue` with a negative `--days` or a bad `--as-of` exits with 1, prints nothing on stdout and `stockroom: error: MESSAGE` on stderr

interpretations: An open or paid order is overdue only when it is more than `days` days old; exactly `days` days old is not overdue (as stated)
An order exactly `days` days old is already overdue, or shipped orders count too (contradicts the stated rule)
